pairs.question: Et, quod maxime mirandum fateor fore, qualiter ad definitum locum vel certe ad statutam diem et horam venire poterant, cum nec idem Karolus, ubi se suosque oporteret, sciebat?
pairs.answer: Quem quidem eventum haud aliter quam munere ac nutu divino visum est evenire potuisse.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question (how the messengers bearing the regalia could reach the appointed place at the appointed day and hour, when not even Charles knew where he would be) immediately answered by the author himself in the next sentence: that this outcome could only have come about by divine gift and will. The preceding rhetorical exclamation 'Quis non miretur... valuisse?' is dropped because it is a pure wonder-question (expecting 'no one') with no substantive author-supplied answer. Answer window stops at the first full stop; what follows ('ac per hoc commilitonibus stuporem iniecit...') is narrative elaboration on its effect, not part of the answer.
